The GPU and the NPU at the same time, measured

For four weeks the fleet that works on this engine ran every NPU job behind the GPU queue. The reason was a report from another project's documentation: GPU and NPU work at the same time could hang the machine, or corrupt NPU results, while the GPU's fabric clock (FCLK) changed level. The suggested fix was to hold FCLK at its top level. We never reproduced it; we just avoided it.

The hybrid route (the prompt on the NPU, the tokens on the GPU) needs both devices busy at once, so the question had to be settled by measurement.

Method#

The NPU side is the kernel arena's byte-exact oracle: one real decode kernel of the 27B ternary model, five launches per cell, every output compared byte for byte against the frozen reference. The GPU side is a looping llama-bench on HRX (prefill 512, decode 128) started before the NPU runs and kept running through them. Four cells, GPU idle or busy times FCLK on auto or held at the top level, run twice, with the live FCLK level sampled once a second and the kernel log checked for GPU resets, MODE2 resets and ring timeouts after every cell. The hold cells ran last, and the box was returned to auto and verified before the run was called done.

Result#

cell ms per launch, median GB/s FCLK levels seen byte-exact resets
GPU idle, FCLK auto 10.79 8.26 5, 6 and 7, changing mid-run 5 of 5 0
GPU idle, FCLK held 10.92 8.16 7 5 of 5 0
GPU busy, FCLK auto 12.04 7.40 6 and 7, changing mid-run 5 of 5 0
GPU busy, FCLK held 12.01 7.42 7 5 of 5 0

Forty reps in total, twenty of them with the GPU busy, 160 byte-exact checks, all passing, and zero reset or timeout lines in the kernel log in any cell, with the fabric clock demonstrably changing level in the middle of NPU runs. Kernel 7.3.0-rc4 with the IOMMU PerfOpt backports, SMU firmware 100.7.0, BIOS 1.09.

So: the hazard does not reproduce on this kernel and firmware. A busy GPU costs the NPU about 13 % of its weight stream, through shared memory bandwidth, and nothing else. The first pass had suggested that holding FCLK removes that cost; the second pass did not confirm it, so that claim is retracted and the box stays on auto.

What changed because of it#

NPU jobs no longer queue behind GPU jobs on the development box; they take the NPU device lock only. Every arena score now records whether the GPU was busy during the launch, so a 13 % dip is never mistaken for a kernel regression. And the hybrid route is planned around a measured 13 %, not around a hang. The full table is in Hybrid.

Sources: engine #673, Hybrid.
